Hospitalization was reported by a substantially higher percentage of pregnant women (31.5%) than nonpregnant women (5.8%)
Sixteen deaths (0.2%) were reported among 8,207 pregnant women, and 208 (0.2%) were reported among 83,205 nonpregnant women.
Among pregnant women, 46.2% were Hispanic, 23.0% were non-Hispanic white (white), 22.1% were non-Hispanic black (black)
Pregnant women were admitted more frequently to the ICU (1.5%) than were nonpregnant women (0.9%).
After adjusting for age, presence of underlying conditions, and race/ethnicity
When stratified by race/ethnicity, ICU admission was most frequently reported among pregnant women who were non-Hispanic Asian (3.5%)
Data on laboratory-confirmed and probable COVID-19 cases † were electronically reported to CDC

methods_quotes.q: Crude and adjusted risk ratios and 95% CIs for outcomes were calculated using modified Poisson regression.
Risk ratios were adjusted for age (as a continuous variable), presence of underlying chronic conditions (yes/no), and race/ethnicity.
Outcomes with missing data were assumed not to have occurred
